summary: QA pass on Trusted Circle Recipient flow (flag EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT now true). Scoped-permission visibility, accept/decline, revoke, and no-expiry were verified live via API (requests) with Create->GET persistence checks, plus one live-UI pass (login + invite screen) via Playwright. Core permission-gating logic is correct and was independently confirmed both in code and live on the recipient's invite screen. However found 2 CRITICAL gaps vs the requested scenarios: (1) the owner-side UI has NO revoke button and NO permission-selection control at all (both only exist as backend endpoints / hardcoded defaults), so 'owner selects specific permissions' and 'owner revokes from trusted-circle.tsx' could NOT be exercised through the UI as specified — backend endpoints themselves work correctly when called directly. (2) /api/alerts and /api/alerts/{id} leak payload.last_location.area to the recipient's raw API response even when temp_location permission is False — enforcement of that permission is currently client-side only (alerts/[id].tsx hides it visually) not server-side. Also found a UI regression: a 'Choose your language' modal persistently overlays screens during this test session and intercepted the Accept button tap (live UI accept attempt did not register; confirmed via API recheck that status stayed 'pending'). No expiry mechanism exists in trusted_circle_links at all (no expires_at field, no code path checks it) — pending invites never expire.

critical.issue: payload.last_location.area (human-readable last known location, e.g. 'QA Secret Area 3') is returned in the raw JSON response to the recipient even when the link's permissions.temp_location is False. Verified live: created an accepted link with temp_location:false, created a journey, PATCHed a location update, triggered a help_requested alert -> GET /api/alerts/{id} returned payload.last_location.area despite permissions.temp_location=false. Raw lat/lng are correctly never included (confirmed in journey_router.py _notify_linked_recipients, which only forwards 'area', not lat/lng) so the raw-coordinate leak specifically asked about is NOT present, but a location-name leak is. Enforcement of temp_location is currently done ONLY on the frontend (alerts/[id].tsx checks perms.temp_location before rendering) — not server-side.

minor.issue: Every created alert/invite ends in state 'FAILED' (push send failed, non-fatal per design) in this preview env — real push delivery to recipients cannot be verified here; likely SuprSend relay unreachable from preview.

ui_bugs.issue: No UI exists for the owner to revoke a sent/accepted connection. revokeInvitation() is exported from src/trustedCircle/api.ts but is never imported or called anywhere in the frontend. There is also no list of sent invitations with their status on this screen.

Owner has no UI control to choose which permissions to grant. The invite button calls inviteContact(authToken, { name, phone }) with NO permissions argument, so every invite silently uses the backend PermissionsIn defaults (journey_status/expected_arrival/missed_checkin/emergency_requests=True, temp_location=False). The reviewed scenario 'owner selects a specific subset of permissions' cannot be performed via the app UI at all.

A 'Choose your language' modal appeared stacked on top of invite detail, alerts inbox and home screens repeatedly during this automated session and intercepted a tap on testID=invite-accept (API recheck confirmed invite status stayed 'pending' after the tap). Could be a genuine overlay/z-index regression or an environment-specific one-time prompt that is mis-triggering on every route change; worth a quick look since it blocks taps on underlying controls.

integration_issues.issue: Tapping Accept via Playwright did not transition the invite out of 'pending' (blocked by the overlay above). Backend respond endpoint itself was separately verified correct via direct API calls (pytest: accept -> 200, status accepted, persisted on reload; double-respond -> 400).

scenario_results.owner_creates_scoped_invite: PARTIAL - verified via direct API call only (no UI control exists to pick permissions); not exercisable through the app as requested
scenario_results.recipient_sees_only_granted_permissions: PASS - verified live via UI: invite screen showed ONLY 'Journey status updates' and 'Expected arrival time' text; no mention/affordance anywhere for temp_location or emergency_requests. Also confirmed via code (Object.entries(PERM_LABEL).map renders conditionally per perms[key]) and via API (GET invitation returns temp_location:false, emergency_requests:false).
scenario_results.recipient_accept: PASS via API (status pending->accepted, persisted); BLOCKED via live UI tap due to overlay interception
scenario_results.recipient_decline: PASS via API (fresh invite -> decline -> status 'declined', persisted, no further pending actions)
scenario_results.coordinate_location_denial: PASS for raw GPS lat/lng (never sent to recipients by design, confirmed in code). FAIL for location-name leak: payload.last_location.area is present in raw API responses even with temp_location=false (see backend critical issue above). Frontend correctly hides it from the rendered UI, so a typical user would not see it, but the data is technically exposed over the API.
scenario_results.temp_location_granted_journey_active_gat: PARTIALLY VERIFIED - triggered a real journey + location update + help_requested alert with temp_location granted on a separate link (not shown in detail above but same mechanism); last_location.area appears in payload once a location update has occurred, consistent with 'only while journey active' intent. Could not fully trigger the no-active-journey case distinctly within budget.
scenario_results.link_revocation: Backend PASS (owner revoke -> 200, recipient GET shows status 'revoked', non-owner cannot revoke -> 403). Frontend BLOCKED - no revoke UI exists on trusted-circle.tsx.
scenario_results.link_expiry: NOT IMPLEMENTED - no expires_at/expiry field in trusted_circle_links schema or any router logic; a pending invite never expires server-side. Confirmed by code review and live API check (GET invitation never returns an expiry field).
scenario_results.alerts_inbox_invitations_tab: PASS - live UI: /alerts with Invitations tab correctly lists pending invitations ('Trusted Circle invitation · From <owner>') alongside other alert types in the 'All' tab.
scenario_results.regression_navigation: PASS (light check) - login redirected to /home successfully; bottom tab testids present and intact (tab-home, tab-rights, tab-ask, tab-myfiles, tab-me). Did not deep-test NotificationTapBridge push-tap behavior (out of scope for this budget / requires real push tap simulation).

action_items: CRITICAL: Build owner-side revoke UI on trusted-circle.tsx (call revokeInvitation from src/trustedCircle/api.ts) — currently unreachable from the app.

CRITICAL: Build owner-side permission-selection UI before sending an invite — currently inviteContact() always uses hardcoded backend defaults; no way for a real user to grant/withhold temp_location or emergency_requests from the app.

HIGH: Server-side filter payload.last_location out of GET /api/alerts and /api/alerts/{id} responses when the link's permissions.temp_location is False (mirror the access_revoked stripping pattern already in alerts_router.get_alert). Do not rely on frontend-only hiding for a privacy-sensitive field.

HIGH: Investigate the 'Choose your language' modal appearing stacked over invite/alerts/home screens during navigation and intercepting taps on testID=invite-accept — reproduce and fix the overlay/z-index or trigger condition.
MEDIUM: Decide if a link-expiry mechanism (expires_at + background check or check-on-read) is in-scope for this feature; currently pending invites live forever.
LOW: Push delivery state is 'FAILED' for all generated alerts/invites in this preview env — confirm whether this is expected (no relay configured) or needs investigation before going live.
critical_code_review_comments: trusted_circle_router.py and alerts_router.py are clean, async, and use Depends(current_user) consistently with proper 403/404 handling and no leaked _id — good baseline.

alerts_router.get_alert() already has the right pattern for stripping data on revocation (out['payload'] = {} when link not accepted) — the same pattern should be extended to strip last_location when temp_location permission is false, for both list_alerts and get_alert.
trusted_circle_router.py has zero expiry-related fields/logic; if link expiry is a hard requirement it needs net-new schema (expires_at) and a check in respond()/get_invitation().

Frontend trusted-circle.tsx's TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT block only renders a one-shot 'Invite' link per local contact with no follow-up state (no owner visibility into pending/accepted/revoked invites at all) — this is a significant UX gap now that the flag is on.

success_rate.backend: 100% (5/5 custom QA tests passed; findings documented as design/security observations, not test failures)
success_rate.frontend: ~40% (permission-visibility and alerts-inbox verified live; accept-tap, revoke-UI, and permission-selection-UI could not be completed/do not exist)

Not cleaned up — low risk since these are throwaway dev-preview QA accounts already used for other testing per /app/memory/test_credentials.md.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Flag EXPO_PUBLIC_TRUSTED_CIRCLE_RECIPIENT is currently 'true' in frontend/.env for this QA pass per explicit user instruction — do NOT assume it should stay on; main agent must report back to user to decide keep-on vs revert. If kept on, the two CRITICAL frontend gaps (no revoke UI, no permission-picker UI) mean real users cannot use the owner side of this feature meaningfully yet even though backend is solid. Re-run /app/backend/tests/test_trusted_circle_qa_pass.py after any fix (requires EXPO_BACKEND_URL env var exported from frontend/.env's EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL before invoking pytest, since BASE_URL reads EXPO_BACKEND_URL not EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL).
rca_of_issue: Location-name leak RCA: _notify_linked_recipients() in journey_router.py builds the alert payload directly from rec['last_location'] without checking the target link's permissions.temp_location at all (it only checks link.status=='accepted' and link.invitee_user_id inside create_alert_and_notify). The permission is enforced only by the UI layer (alerts/[id].tsx's `perms.temp_location && loc && loc.area` guard and invite/[id].tsx's conditional PERM_LABEL rendering), never by the API. Fix: in alerts_router.py's list_alerts and get_alert, after resolving the link, pop/clear payload['last_location'] when link.permissions.get('temp_location') is falsy, same place access_revoked already clears payload.
